original_question: Let (u_i)_{i >= 1} be a strictly increasing sequence of integers greater than 1. Construct a sieve by, at step i, keeping one number among the next u_i - 1 remaining numbers and deleting every u_i-th remaining number. What relationship between the generator sequence (u_i) and the resulting remaining sequence can be proved?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core data and mechanism of Item 31: a strictly increasing sequence (u_i) with u_i > 1, a stage-by-stage sieve on the natural numbers in which one admissible survivor is kept at each stage and every u_i-th surviving term is deleted, and the fact that the paper asks for a relationship between the generator sequence and the sequence that remains.
missing_details: The sieve starts specifically from the natural numbers N = {1,2,3,...}, not from an arbitrary ambient set.
The first stage is stated separately in the paper: keep one number among 1,2,...,u_1-1, then delete every u_1-th number.
At each later stage, the operation is performed on the current remaining sequence, taken in its natural increasing order.

Item 31 does not specify which admissible number is kept at stage i; this hidden choice is part of the ambiguity of the problem. The nearby discussion in Item 30 says the kept number may be any element of the relevant block, and Item 32 makes this explicit by introducing a second sequence v_i.
The paper explicitly calls (u_i) the "sieve generator."
The paper does not state a theorem, conjecture, or specific formula here; it poses an open-ended problem to "study the relationship" between the generator and the residual sequence.
To make the question stand-alone, one should specify that the "remaining sequence" means the increasing sequence of integers surviving after all stages of the sieve.
refined_question: Let (u_i)_{i>=1} be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with u_i > 1. Starting from the natural numbers N = {1,2,3,...}, perform the following general-sequence sieve: at stage 1, keep one number among 1,2,...,u_1-1 and delete every u_1-th number; inductively, at stage k >= 2, from the current increasing sequence of survivors keep one number among the next u_k-1 remaining numbers and delete every u_k-th remaining number. The sequence (u_i) is called the sieve generator. Study the relationship between the sieve generator (u_i) and the increasing sequence of integers that remains after this sieve is carried out.
justification: The draft is targeting Item 31 almost verbatim: the paper's official wording is "Problem: study the relationship between sequence u_i ... and the remaining sequence resulted from the general sieve." I therefore kept the scope narrow and did not replace it by a broader sieve question. I used the introduction to confirm that the paper is a compendium of unsolved problems rather than a theorem-driven article, Item 30 to recover the hidden assumption that the kept element at each stage is not fixed and may be chosen arbitrarily, and Item 32 to verify that making the kept position explicit would require adding a second sequence v_i. The refined version only adds the implicit setup needed to make Item 31 mathematically stand-alone.
